world.name: The Bell Beneath Blackwater — DM Audit
world.description: At low tide, a bell rings from a chapel swallowed by the sea. A fishing crew returns with no memory of seven missing days. The harbor guild wants the matter quiet before the Lantern Festival.

blocks.text: A salt-stained harbor on [[The Bell Coast]], where canal bridges link crowded markets and fishing quays. [[Mara Vell]] runs the harbor office, [[Brother Orin]] keeps the shrine, and [[Nella Reed]] knows the hidden waterways.
Blue nets drying on railings, brass lanterns above every doorway, gulls wheeling over the customs house. At low tide, a bell sounds from beyond the harbor mouth.
[[Mara Vell]], [[Brother Orin]], and [[Nella Reed]]. The [[Tidemarket Guild]] controls the warehouses.
SECRET AUDIT: The old bell tower points to the vault beneath [[The Sunken Chapel]]. The Choir Below has hidden a cache in Lantern Ward.
Keeper of the shrine to [[The Drowned Lantern]] in [[Blackwater]]. Offers tea before answering questions. He remembers the chapel bell ringing once before, on the night his sister vanished.

On 14 Lanternfall, the people of [[Blackwater]] float lanterns for sailors who never returned. [[Brother Orin]] leads the blessing of [[The Drowned Lantern]], while [[Mara Vell]] opens the market. The missing crew must be found before the bell rings at dusk.

Seven days have vanished from the memories of the crew who came ashore this morning. Nella Reed is waiting by the east quay; she remembers a bell beneath the water, and nothing after it.

Find Brother Orin before the Lantern Festival. Ask him why the chapel bell is ringing when the tide has swallowed its tower. Take the Saltglass Key from my office, but keep it wrapped until you reach the causeway.

Bring our people home before the festival bell sounds at dusk. The harbor will stand behind you.
SECRET AUDIT: Mara knows the Choir Below’s password is seven silent tides.
Harbormaster of [[Blackwater]] and public face of the [[Tidemarket Guild]]. She hires the party to locate the missing crew before the Lantern Festival.
A weather-beaten woman in a blue oilskin coat, with a silver whistle and salt-stiff hair.
Clipped sentences; taps her whistle when worried. Practical, protective of the dockworkers, impatient with noble patrons.
Mara secretly paid [[Nella Reed]] to recover the [[Saltglass Key]]. She knows the missing crew heard the bell beneath [[The Sunken Chapel]].
A cheerful smuggler who pilots a skiff through the flooded alleys of [[Blackwater]]. Owes [[Mara Vell]] a favor. Her latest cargo was the [[Saltglass Key]].
Nella saw a masked member of [[The Choir Below]] beside [[The Sunken Chapel]]. She will talk only if the party promises safe passage for her brother.
Entrusted to Tessa by Mara Vell.
A translucent green key, warm to the touch, with teeth shaped like waves. Salt water beads on it even when dry. Found in [[Nella Reed]]’s cargo.
Campaign opening: [[Tessa Brine]] arrives in [[Blackwater]] two days before the [[Lantern Festival]]. [[Mara Vell]] offers work investigating [[The Bell Beneath the Bay]].

- Interview [[Nella Reed]] about the missing seven days.
- Ask [[Brother Orin]] why the drowned bell still rings.
- Find what the [[Saltglass Key]] opens in [[The Sunken Chapel]].

SECRET AUDIT: Start at the harbor office, follow the crew to the chapel, then reveal the lower crypt. [[The Choir Below]] will try to steal the key if the party delays. Keep one captured sailor alive to explain the missing days.

rows.name: Choir lookout
rows.conditions: Frightened; tries to flee toward the chapel.

features.name: Darkvision
features.text: You have Darkvision with a range of 120 feet.

features.name: Dwarven Resilience
features.text: You have Resistance to Poison damage. You also have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.

features.name: Dwarven Toughness
features.text: Your Hit Point maximum increases by 1, and it increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level.

features.name: Stonecunning
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you gain Tremorsense with a range of 60 feet for 10 minutes. You must be on a stone surface or touching a stone surface to use this Tremorsense. The stone can be natural or worked.

You can use this Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.text:
You have honed your martial prowess and gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. Defense is recommended.

Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

features.name: Second Wind
features.text:
You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a Bonus Action, you can use it to regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level.

You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter Features table.

features.name: Weapon Mastery
features.text:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Fighter Features table.

features.name: Savage Attacker
features.text: You've trained to deal particularly damaging strikes. Once per turn when you hit a target with a weapon, you can roll the weapon's damage dice twice and use either roll against the target.

features.name: Defense
features.text: While you're wearing Light, Medium, or Heavy armor, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class.

features.name: Weapon Mastery
features.text: Greatsword, flail and spear. Former harbor watch; trained to fight on narrow quays.

features.name: Action Surge
features.text:
You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the Magic action.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest but only once on a turn.

features.name: Tactical Mind
features.text: You have a mind for tactics on and off the battlefield. When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself toward success. Rather than regaining Hit Points, you roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn't expended.

personality.traits: Counts exits before sitting down; always carries spare rope.
personality.ideals: No crew member gets left behind.
personality.bonds: Mara Vell once saved her from a shipwreck.
personality.flaws: Distrusts anyone who keeps their hands hidden.

data.notes: A former harbor watch soldier from Blackwater, looking for Nella Reed’s missing crew. Proficient with a dragonchess set.

fields.Stakes: The crew may lose their memories permanently
fields.Next lead: Talk to Nella at the east docks

blocks.text: [[Mara Vell]] offers 50 gp to find the missing crew. Speak with [[Nella Reed]] at the docks and [[Brother Orin]] at the shrine. Follow the bell to [[The Sunken Chapel]] before the Lantern Festival.
SECRET AUDIT: The masked choir erased the crew’s memories. They plan to sound the drowned bell during the Lantern Festival and open the vault under [[The Sunken Chapel]].
Patron of lost sailors and promises kept in darkness. Worshippers float lanterns on the harbor at the Lantern Festival. [[Brother Orin]] tends the last shrine in [[Blackwater]].
A ruined chapel on a tidal islet outside [[Blackwater]]. At low tide a causeway reaches the broken doors. The vault below still holds a bell dedicated to [[The Drowned Lantern]].
Barnacled pews, green light under the altar, and wet footprints leading down dry stairs. A rope descends into a shaft where the bell should be.
SECRET AUDIT: The [[Saltglass Key]] opens the drowned reliquary. [[The Choir Below]] is keeping the missing crew in the lower crypt.
The shipowners, fishmongers and porters who keep [[Blackwater]] fed. Their representative is [[Mara Vell]]. The Lantern Festival is their most profitable week.
Keep trade moving, return the missing crew, and prevent panic. Pay discreet troubleshooters rather than call the militia.
